anchors.statement: The template ships general database commands on the CLI, MCP, and HTTP, including delete row <table> <id>. The consumer can disable that surface. An application command calls the same backend operation through its own CLI command, MCP tool, and HTTP route.
anchors.quote: the 'general database commands' would be expected to be disabled by the customer. they are simply a bootstrap tool and could easily be 'replaced' w/ a command that has better ux and does a similar call on the back-end. i.e. delete row <table> <id> would be a general command which could be used 'under the hood' w/ a different cli/mcp/http call.
anchors.summary: Bootstrap database commands the consumer can disable
anchors.scope: a bead that edits template CLI, MCP, or HTTP commands
anchors.deterministic_check: The generated template registers a general delete-row command on the CLI, on MCP, and over HTTP, and a generation flag omits those three registrations while the backend operation remains callable.
